text: The manufacturer shall ensure that the AEBS is operational whenever the vehicle ignition is in the ON state and vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h and less than or equal to 60 km/h unless deactivation is explicitly permitted under Section 3.4.
The system shall provide a visual warning to the driver at least 1.4 seconds before the initiation of automatic braking when a critical object is detected in the forward field of view.
The system shall log activation of automatic braking to non-volatile memory.
The system shall log driver override of automatic braking to non-volatile memory.
The system shall log system failure as defined in 2.4 to non-volatile memory.
The system shall log temporary deactivation by the driver to non-volatile memory.
Deactivation shall not persist across ignition cycles unless the driver explicitly confirms deactivation at each new ignition cycle.
The system shall detect an adult pedestrian target crossing the vehicle path at 5 km/h lateral speed in daylight conditions with a detection rate of not less than 95% over 20 consecutive test runs.
The system shall detect the same target in night conditions with a detection rate of not less than 90% over 20 consecutive test runs.
False positive rate shall not exceed 1 event per 100 km during normal urban driving as defined in Annex 3, Table A.1.
The system shall detect a cyclist travelling parallel to the subject vehicle at a lateral offset of 1.0 m when relative speed is between 10 km/h and 40 km/h.
When partial sensor occlusion of at least 30% is detected, the system shall inform the driver within 3 seconds via a yellow tell-tale.
The system shall not silently disable automatic braking without driver notification.

Upon detection of a critical object with TTC less than or equal to 1.8 s, the system shall initiate automatic braking to achieve a deceleration of at least 6 m/s^2 on dry pavement unless limited by Section 4.3.
The system shall release automatic braking within 500 ms after the driver applies accelerator pedal input exceeding 50% of full travel.
The system shall store the last 50 AEBS events including timestamp, vehicle speed, TTC at warning, TTC at braking, object classification, and sensor health bitmask.
Log retention shall survive loss of primary vehicle power for a minimum of 72 hours using a backup power source or non-volatile storage.
Personal data shall not be stored in event logs unless required for homologation and in compliance with applicable privacy regulations.
The software safety requirements shall be derived from the technical safety requirements and the system architectural design.
Each software safety requirement shall be uniquely identifiable.
Each software safety requirement shall be traceable to at least one technical safety requirement.
Each software safety requirement shall be verifiable by analysis, review, or test.
Ambiguous terms shall not be used without quantified criteria.
Safety-related software components shall be separated from non-safety-related software components to the extent required by the ASIL of the item.
Freedom from interference shall be ensured between software elements with different ASIL assignments, or evidence shall be provided that interference is controlled.
Coding guidelines shall address language subset such as MISRA C:2012.
Software unit verification shall provide evidence that the software units fulfil their software unit requirements.
Failed tests shall be analyzed, classified, and resolved before release of the software to integration testing.
All safety-related software artifacts shall be placed under configuration management before verification activities commence.
Each change to safety-related software shall undergo impact analysis, approval by the functional safety manager or delegate, and updated verification evidence as determined by the impact analysis.

The manufacturer shall ensure that systems remain operational during normal operating conditions and shall not design systems to depend on continuous connectivity to external networks for core safety functions.
The warning tell-tale symbol shall conform to ISO 2575 symbol ID P-087 or subsequent revision accepted by the type-approval authority.
The system shall remain enabled by default at each ignition cycle.
Type-approval testing shall include scenarios AEBS-01 through AEBS-05 as defined in UN R152 Annex 2 or equivalent scenarios accepted by the authority.
Where event data recorders are fitted, AEBS activation events shall be recorded with time stamp, vehicle speed, brake pedal status, AEBS state, and longitudinal acceleration.
Personal identifiers shall not be written to the public EDR dataset accessible during roadside inspection.
The manufacturer shall demonstrate that series-produced vehicles conform to the approved type with respect to each fitted system in Section B.
Software updates affecting safety systems shall be notified to the authority when they alter type-approved behavior unless covered by a prior agreement on over-the-air update governance.
